title: White Tie Attire
metaTitle: White Tie Attire: What Women and Men Wear, vs Black Tie
metaDescription: White tie attire is the most formal dress code: a floor-length gown for women; tailcoat, white vest and white bow tie for men. How it differs from black tie.
h1: White Tie Attire for Women and Men: The Most Formal Dress Code
answer: White tie is the most formal dress code there is. Women wear a floor-length evening gown, with long gloves optional. Men wear a black tailcoat with matching trousers, a stiff white piqué wing-collar shirt with studs and cufflinks, a white vest, a white bow tie, white or gray gloves, and black patent shoes with black socks. A tuxedo is not white tie.
intro: White tie attire is full evening dress: the one dress code with no room for interpretation and no shorter, simpler version. That is what makes it easier than it looks. The garment list is fixed, and both the women's and the men's halves fit on an index card. The difficulty is practical, not conceptual. Almost nobody owns a tailcoat, very few people have been to a white tie event, and the invitation tends to arrive for a once-in-a-lifetime occasion where getting it wrong feels expensive. This guide gives the exact list for women and men, shows how white tie differs from black tie item by item, and covers what to do when you are unsure.

contentSections.heading: The full white tie list, for women and for men
contentSections.content:
The Emily Post Institute describes white tie as the most formal dress code, usually reserved for high-profile or royal events. Its list is short and specific.

For women:
• A floor-length evening gown.
• Long gloves, which Emily Post lists as optional.

For men:
• A black tailcoat with matching trousers. Emily Post notes the trousers carry one satin or braid stripe down the outer seam in the US and two in Europe and the UK.
• A stiff-fronted white piqué shirt with a wing collar, worn with studs and cufflinks.
• Braces (suspenders) to hold the trousers.
• A white vest (waistcoat) and a white bow tie.
• White or gray gloves.
• Black patent shoes with black socks.

Wikipedia's White tie article adds the traditional optional extras: for men, a black top hat, a white scarf, a pocket watch, a white pocket square and a boutonnière; for women, evening gloves, jewelry, a small handbag and, optionally, a tiara. It also notes that orders, decorations and medals may be worn in miniature, which is why you will see them at state banquets.

One small disagreement between the two sources is worth knowing about if you are buying rather than renting. Wikipedia describes the trousers with galon, a braid of two silk stripes, while Emily Post says the two-stripe version is European and British and the American version has one. If you hire a tailcoat, take whatever stripe the trousers come with: no one at the event will count them.

Notice what is absent from the women's list. There is no cocktail dress, no little black dress, no dressy separates and no midi. Every other formal code allows at least one of those. White tie does not, and that single fact settles most women's questions about it.

contentSections.heading: White tie vs black tie, item by item
contentSections.content:
The quickest way to understand white tie is to put it next to black tie, the code most people already know. The two share the same black-and-white palette and the same black patent shoes, which is why they get confused. The difference is in four places on a man and in one place on a woman.

On a man, white tie means tails instead of a tuxedo jacket, a white vest instead of a black cummerbund or vest, a white bow tie instead of a black one, and gloves, which black tie does not use at all. The shirt is stiffer too: a starched piqué front and a wing collar, where black tie takes a formal white shirt with a turndown collar.

On a woman, the gown is the whole difference. Black tie lets a woman choose a floor-length gown, a dressy cocktail dress or her dressiest little black dress. White tie leaves only the gown. Gloves are optional at both, but they are far more common at white tie.

The practical consequence: a woman who owns a black tie gown already has a white tie outfit, while a man who owns a tuxedo does not. A tuxedo with a white bow tie is still a tuxedo.

contentSections.heading: How rare is a white tie wedding?
contentSections.content:
Very. Wikipedia's article lists the places white tie survives: state banquets and investitures, the Nobel Banquet in Stockholm, the Vienna Opera Ball, Mardi Gras balls in New Orleans, the May and Commemoration balls at Cambridge and Oxford, the Al Smith Memorial Dinner in New York, some university ceremonies in Scandinavia and the Netherlands, and traditional weddings and church celebrations.

Our own data shows how seldom it reaches ordinary guests. In our analysis of 10,700 posts on r/Weddingattireapproval (16 April – 21 October 2026), we searched each post's title and body text for a set of keywords and counted each post once per topic; posts that are only a photo carry no body text, so every count is a floor, not a ceiling. Only 16 of the 10,700 posts mention white tie at all, about 0.1%. By comparison, 1,605 posts mention black tie and 599 mention black tie optional. Even within the forum's own Black/White Tie category, 9 of 1,307 posts name white tie; the rest are about black tie.

What that means for you: if a wedding invitation really says white tie, the couple chose those words on purpose. It is not a loose synonym for "dress up." Treat the list above as the requirement, and if you suspect the hosts meant black tie, ask them before you rent tails rather than after.

contentSections.heading: Choosing a white tie gown: length, cover and color
contentSections.content:
"Floor-length" means what it says. A gown that stops at the ankle reads as a long dress, not as evening dress, and a high-low hem or a midi is a cocktail silhouette. Let the hem reach the top of your shoe when you stand in the heels you will wear.

Beyond length, a few decisions matter more than they would at black tie:
• Gloves. Emily Post calls long gloves optional; Wikipedia lists evening gloves as part of the women's outfit. If you want to wear them, white tie is the one occasion where nobody will think they are a costume.
• Shoulders and the ceremony. Emily Post's wedding-guest advice asks guests to consider whether bare shoulders suit a religious ceremony. Many white tie weddings are traditional church weddings, so a strapless gown usually needs a wrap, stole or bolero for the service.
• Color. White tie restricts the man's palette, not yours. Any rich color works, and black is entirely appropriate at an evening event of this formality. The color to avoid is white or anything close to it at a wedding; see our guide to wedding guest dress colors to avoid.
• Fabric. Formality shows in the fabric as much as the cut. Satin, silk crepe, velvet in winter and heavy chiffon read as evening wear; cotton jersey and printed day fabrics do not, however long they are.
• Jewelry and tiaras. Wikipedia lists a tiara among the optional accessories. At a wedding, most guests leave the tiara at home so they do not compete with the bride; fine earrings or a necklace do the job.

Women sometimes ask whether an evening trouser suit can work. Emily Post's white tie list contains only the gown, so if you prefer trousers, ask the hosts first. That is the only case on this page where asking is not optional.

contentSections.heading: Getting the men's side right without owning tails
contentSections.content:
Few men own white tie, and nobody expects them to. The normal route is hiring the whole outfit from a formalwear specialist: tailcoat, trousers, shirt, vest, bow tie and often the studs and braces as a set. Book early. White tie stock is small compared with tuxedo stock, and the dates that need it, such as balls, galas and the holiday season, tend to cluster.

When you collect it, check four things:
• The coat is a tailcoat, cut short at the front with tails behind, not a tuxedo jacket.
• The vest and bow tie are white. A black vest or black bow tie under tails is a half-and-half outfit that is neither code.
• The shirt has a wing collar and a stiff front with stud holes, and you have studs and cufflinks to go in them.
• You have braces. The trousers are not made to take a belt.

Add white or gray gloves and black patent shoes with black socks, which completes Emily Post's list. If you have military, civic or order decorations, Wikipedia notes that miniatures may be worn with white tie.

If a tailcoat truly is not possible, do not quietly swap in a tuxedo. Tell the hosts and let them decide. They may well tell you a tuxedo is fine. A guest who asked looks considerate; a guest who improvised looks like he misread the invitation.

contentSections.heading: When you're unsure, or the invitation says "white tie optional"
contentSections.content:
Start with the invitation itself. Exact wording matters at this level: "white tie" and "white tie optional" mean different things, and "formal" or "black tie" mean something else again.

"White tie optional" does not appear in Emily Post's attire guide. Read it on the same pattern as black tie optional, where the stricter code is welcome and the next code down is acceptable: tails are welcome, and a tuxedo is fine. For women this changes almost nothing. A floor-length gown is correct at both white tie and black tie, so it is the safe choice whichever way the hosts lean.

If you still cannot tell, the sequence is simple:
• Check the wedding website. Couples who choose white tie usually explain it there.
• Ask the couple or a member of the wedding party. A short question weeks ahead is better than a guess.
• If you cannot ask, dress to the stricter reading: a gown for women, tails for men if you can hire them.

The common mistakes at white tie are all variations of one error, treating it as black tie with extras:
• A tuxedo with a white bow tie.
• A cocktail dress or a midi, however dressy.
• A black vest or cummerbund under tails.
• A belt instead of braces.
• Skipping the wrap for a church ceremony in a strapless gown.

For the whole ladder from casual to white tie, start with our wedding dress codes explained hub.

faqs.question: What is white tie attire for a woman?
faqs.answer: A floor-length evening gown. Emily Post lists long gloves as an optional addition; Wikipedia adds jewelry, a small handbag and, optionally, a tiara. Cocktail dresses, little black dresses and midis are not white tie.

faqs.question: Does white tie mean you have to wear white?
faqs.answer: No. The name comes from the man's white bow tie and white vest. Women can wear any color that suits an evening event, though white and near-white are still best avoided at a wedding.

faqs.question: Is white tie more formal than black tie?
faqs.answer: Yes. White tie is the most formal dress code there is; black tie is the next step down. Black tie allows a tuxedo and, for women, dressy cocktail dresses. White tie requires tails and a floor-length gown.

faqs.question: Where can you buy or rent white tie attire?
faqs.answer: Men usually rent the full outfit from a formalwear rental shop or a tailor that keeps evening wear. Buying makes sense only if you expect several white tie events. Women can wear any floor-length evening gown, including one bought for a black tie event.
